text:
mira: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small refactor: split long generation requests into "parcels" (token-aligned chunks) so the scheduler can admit and prefetch per-parcel instead of the whole sequence. reduces peak headroom and lets us interleave smaller work. thoughts?

alex: hm, interesting. how do you define parcel boundaries? always fixed-size tokens?

mira: not fixed. idea is horizon-based: admit first N tokens as parcel0, prefetch KV for parcel0 + H horizon, then admit next parcel when parcel0 is executing or when headroom frees. horizon is tunable by model/workload.

diego: tradeoffs: + lower instantaneous memory/kv pressure, + better packing for short requests. - potential extra tail latency from parcel reassembly and extra RPCs. need a clear SLO model.

samir: admission surface change concerns me. do we expect callers to be aware of parcels? or transparent at runtime?

mira: transparent. call stays the same. runtime slices internally. only change: scheduler gets parcel-level admission tokens and can return partial "inflight" metrics. callers see one streaming response.

samir: ok, can you sketch the admission API shape so infra can review?

mira: sure. rough idea:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-2b",
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "total_tokens": 1024,
  "parcel_size_hint": 128,        // optional
  "horizon_tokens": 256,         // how far to prefetch ahead
  "slo_profile": "interactive" // maps to headroom policy
}
```

alex: two quick concerns: 1) prefetch + quantized kernels might be wasted if parcels get cancelled. 2) billing/metrics: we need to attribute cost per request, not parcel.

mira: agree both are real. for 1) proposal: keep a short cancellation window for prefetch (evictable horizon). for 2) metrics layer aggregates parcel metrics into the parent request (request_id). will need telemetry changes.

diego: how does this interact with preemption and fallbacks? e.g., if a higher-priority tenant preempts a GPU slot mid-request, do we push remaining parcels to a cheaper variant or region?

mira: yes — parcel-level fallback policy. scheduler can attempt to move remaining parcels to fallback model/region with compatible semantics. cheaper variants get best-effort. this improves graceful degradation (no all-or-nothing).

samir: compatibility with Dedicated/private deployments? customers expect pinned capacity. we must not silently increase inter-datacenter tails.

mira: agreed. for Dedicated we expose a compatibility flag: "parceling_mode: strict" which preserves current semantics (no cross-region migration), but still allows internal parceling for headroom reduction.

deploy-bot: feature-flag "parceling-v1" rolled out to staging at 2024-06-15T14:22Z :rocket:

alex: observability requirements: add headroom_gauge (per-tenant), parcel_latency_histogram, parcel_prefetch_waste_ratio. also an alert if parcel reassembly adds >10% tail to P99 request latency.

diego: experiment plan: A/B on small models first (2b/4b). measure latency tail, cost-per-token, prefetch waste. run for 2 weeks.

mira: action items: (1) i will draft RFC update with API sketch + telemetry table, (2) infra to review admission API and suggest knobs, (3) QA to add reassembly tests, (4) roadmap: opt-in flag -> staging -> canary -> GA.

samir: add a note about billing attribution and logs for debugging cross-parcel hops.

alex: +1 to RFC, add a short compatibility appendix for Dedicated.

mira: thanks everyone. I'll open the RFC PR today and assign reviewers. :pray:

(deploy-bot reaction) :thumbsup:
